_comment: Advisories this repository has looked at, decided about, and cannot currently fix.
This file exists so the CI gate can be a gate. `python -m app.platform.advisories`
fails on ANY advisory against an installed version; without a way to record a
decision, the two upstream-pinned findings below would keep the branch red for
reasons nobody on it can act on, and a permanently-red gate is one people learn to
ignore. So an id listed here stops the CI gate failing, and NOTHING ELSE:
* POST /stack/advisories still reports the package as `vulnerable`, with the CVE.
* The compliance surface still counts it.
An acknowledgement is therefore a statement about the build, never about the risk.
Every entry must name what pins the vulnerable version and what would release it —
an entry whose `blocked_by` has been resolved is a line to delete, not to keep.
Any advisory NOT listed here fails CI. That is the property this file buys.

acknowledged.blocked_by: presidio-anonymizer requires cryptography>=48.0.1,<49.0.0; the fixes land in 49.0.0 and 50.0.0.
acknowledged.assessment: Not reachable from any Aegis code path: the platform uses cryptography only transitively for JWT/TLS primitives, never for PKCS#7 EnvelopedData decryption (GHSA-g6cj) and never for X.509 path building against attacker-supplied intermediates (GHSA-jwv3, GHSA-m2h6). Aegis mints and verifies HS256 tokens, which do not touch either surface.
acknowledged.fix: Upgrade presidio-anonymizer to a release that relaxes the cryptography ceiling, then unpin. Tracked as the PII engine's own upgrade, because dropping presidio changes which PII entities the rail detects.

acknowledged.blocked_by: arize-phoenix pins strawberry-graphql==0.314.3 exactly; the fixes land in 0.315.4 and 0.315.7.
acknowledged.assessment: All three are GraphQL query-complexity or GraphiQL issues (alias-limit bypass, circular-fragment DOS, headers in a GraphiQL URL) reachable only through the Phoenix trace UI, which is an operator-facing observability surface and is not part of the Aegis API. No Aegis route is served by strawberry, and no untrusted party submits GraphQL to this deployment.
acknowledged.fix: Upgrade arize-phoenix once it moves its pin. Aegis does not depend on strawberry directly and has nothing to change itself.
